questions.stem: The INDUS river originates near Lake MANASAROVAR in:
questions.explanation: Indus rises in TIBET near Mt. KAILASH and Lake Mansarovar (Singi Khabab — 'Lion Mouth' spring). Flows NW through Ladakh, Pakistan, Arabian Sea (Karachi). Total length ~3180 km. Right-bank tributaries (less): Kabul. Left-bank (more): JHELUM, CHENAB, RAVI, BEAS, SUTLEJ — the 'PANJ' (5 rivers) of Punjab. Indus Water Treaty (1960) — eastern (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; western (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan. Mansarovar is also source of: Sutlej, Brahmaputra, Karnali (Ghaghara).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The GANGA originates from the GANGOTRI glacier (as Bhagirathi). It officially becomes 'Ganga' after merging with Alaknanda at:

options.option_text: Haridwar, where it leaves the hills

questions.explanation: DEVPRAYAG = confluence of BHAGIRATHI (from Gangotri, Gaumukh) + ALAKNANDA (from Satopanth, Bhagirath Kharak glaciers). Below Devprayag → river is officially called GANGA. Five PRAYAGS (Panch Prayag) of Uttarakhand, in upstream order on Alaknanda: VISHNUPRAYAG (with Dhauliganga) → NANDPRAYAG (with Nandakini) → KARNAPRAYAG (with Pindar) → RUDRAPRAYAG (with Mandakini, from Kedarnath) → DEVPRAYAG (with Bhagirathi). Ganga then enters plains at HARIDWAR.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The BRAHMAPUTRA enters India from China at the border of:
questions.explanation: Brahmaputra (Sanskrit = 'son of Brahma'): in Tibet — TSANGPO (~1700 km along east-west valley north of Himalayas); enters India through ARUNACHAL PRADESH as SIANG / DIHANG (after the great U-bend, Tsangpo gorge — world's deepest). In Assam joins with DIBANG + LOHIT → becomes BRAHMAPUTRA. Length in India ~720 km. Forms world's largest RIVER ISLAND — MAJULI (Assam). In Bangladesh = JAMUNA → meets Padma (Ganga branch) → into Bay of Bengal forming the largest delta on Earth (Sundarbans).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which is the LARGEST tributary of the GANGA, sometimes called the GANGA OF BIHAR?
questions.explanation: YAMUNA — longest + largest tributary of Ganga (~1376 km). Source: Yamunotri glacier. Joins Ganga at PRAYAGRAJ (Allahabad) — TRIVENI SANGAM (with mythical Saraswati). Yamuna's own tributaries: Chambal, Sind, Betwa, Ken (peninsular rivers). Other Ganga tributaries from Himalayas (left bank): Ramganga, GHAGHARA, GANDAK, KOSI. Right bank: Yamuna, SON, Chambal-via-Yamuna. KOSI = 'Sorrow of Bihar' (frequent flooding, channel-shifting). 'Ganga of Bihar' = Ganga itself; 'Yamuna' was meant as longest tributary.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Himalayan rivers are PERENNIAL (flow year-round) because:

options.option_text: They flow through deep canyons always
Fed by glacier melt + monsoon rains
Their basins receive heavy snow only

questions.explanation: Himalayan rivers — PERENNIAL (year-round flow) because of TWO sources: (1) GLACIER + SNOWMELT in summer (when monsoon hasn't started — keeps rivers flowing in pre-monsoon months); (2) MONSOON RAINS in summer + autumn. Peninsular rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery) are mostly RAIN-FED → reduce dramatically in dry season; some smaller streams dry up. Glacier-fed perennial flow is critical for irrigation, drinking water, hydropower in north India. Climate change (faster glacier retreat) → first MORE flow, then less — major future concern.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The river known as the 'SORROW OF BIHAR' due to frequent floods + course changes is:

options.option_text: Tista, sorrow of West Bengal lower

questions.explanation: KOSI — 'Sorrow of Bihar'. Origin: Nepal (Sapt-Kosi = 7 streams from Mt. Everest region). Carries vast silt from young Himalayas → frequently shifts channel (~120 km westward over 200 years). Devastating floods in Bihar's North plains (most famous — 2008 Kosi flood, 3M displaced after embankment breach). Distractor 1 — Damodar = 'Sorrow of Bengal' (now tamed by DVC dams). Distractor 3 — Brahmaputra = 'Sorrow of Assam' (regular floods).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The five 'Panj' tributaries of the Indus (Punjab rivers), from west to east, are:

options.option_text: Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, Jhelum here
Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej (W to E)

questions.explanation: Five rivers of PANJ-AB (= 'five waters'). West → East order: JHELUM → CHENAB → RAVI → BEAS → SUTLEJ. All meet to form PANJNAD, which merges with Indus near Mithankot (Pakistan). Indus Water Treaty (1960, World Bank-brokered): WESTERN rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) → Pakistan; EASTERN rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) → India. India can use western rivers for non-consumptive purposes (hydropower, navigation). Distractor 4 lists Brahmaputra tributaries.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which Himalayan river is older than the Himalayas themselves?

options.option_text: Indus, Brahmaputra, and Sutlej — all antecedent rivers older than the mountain range

questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Indus, Brahmaputra, and Sutlej are antecedent rivers — they predate the Himalayan uplift and cut through the mountains as they rose.

questions.stem: The Brahmaputra river is known by which name in Tibet?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra originates in the Tibetan Plateau near Lake Mansarovar as the Tsangpo and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a RIGHT-BANK tributary of the Ganga?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Yamuna joins the Ganga from the right (south) bank at Prayagraj (Allahabad). Ghaghra, Gandak, and Kosi join from the left (northern/Himalayan) bank.

questions.stem: The Teesta river is a tributary of which major river?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Teesta rises in Sikkim, flows through West Bengal, and joins the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh.

questions.stem: The Indus river originates near which lake in Tibet?

options.option_text: Lake Mansarovar / Sengge Khabab area near Kailash

questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Indus (Sindhu) originates from the Sengge Khabab glaciers near Mount Kailash (Lake Mansarovar region) in Tibet, at an elevation of about 5,000 m.

questions.stem: The Sutlej river, a tributary of the Indus, enters India through which pass?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Sutlej enters India from Tibet through the Shipki La pass in Himachal Pradesh after forming the famous Shipki La gorge.

questions.stem: Which pair of rivers constitutes the boundary between India and Nepal for some distance?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Kali (Mahakali/Sharda) river forms the boundary between India (Uttarakhand) and Nepal for most of its course from the Himalayan glaciers to the plains.

questions.stem: The Ganga river originates from:
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier at Gaumukh in Uttarakhand. The main head stream is the Bhagirathi which merges with the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga.

questions.stem: The five sacred Prayags (confluences) of Uttarakhand lead to Devprayag where which two rivers meet?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi (descending from Gangotri) and the Alaknanda (descending from Badrinath via Vishnuprayag) merge to form the Ganga.

questions.stem: Which river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Kosi river, due to its highly braided nature and frequent course changes, causes devastating floods in Bihar — earning the name 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

questions.stem: The Yamuna river originates from:
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Yamuna originates from Yamunotri Glacier (near Yamunotri temple, Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand) at an elevation of about 6,387 m.

questions.stem: In which state does the Brahmaputra enter India from Tibet?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra (Tsangpo) enters India through Arunachal Pradesh, forming a great gorge near the Namcha Barwa peak, before entering the Assam plains.

questions.stem: The Farakka Barrage on the Ganga is located in:
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Farakka Barrage is located in Murshidabad district, West Bengal, close to the Bangladesh border. It was built to divert Ganga water into the Hooghly to flush Kolkata Port.

questions.stem: The Ravi river is a tributary of the:
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Ravi is one of the five rivers of the Punjab. It joins the Chenab, which joins the Indus in Pakistan.

questions.stem: The Gandak river, a tributary of the Ganga, is called ___ in Nepal.

options.option_text: Narayani (formed by the confluence of Kali Gandaki and Trishuli)

questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Narayani is the main river in Nepal that enters India as the Gandak. It is formed by the Kali Gandaki and Trishuli rivers joining in Nepal.

questions.stem: The Jhelum river originates from:

options.option_text: Verinag spring at the foot of Pir Panjal range (Kashmir Valley)

questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Jhelum originates from the Verinag spring in the Kashmir Valley. It flows through Wular Lake and enters Pakistan before joining the Chenab.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Himalayan river?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Krishna is a peninsular river originating from the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar. Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus are all Himalayan rivers.

questions.stem: The world's highest navigable lake, Lake Mansarovar, is near the source of how many major rivers?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Kailash-Mansarovar region is considered the source area of four great Asian rivers: Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra (Tsangpo), and Karnali (which becomes the Ghaghra/Karnali in India/Nepal).
